commit_message:
[json] Stringfy: Front-load some checks for fast-path

We need to check that we don't have interesting properties (toJSON)
anywhere on JSObject and JSArray prototype chains.
Previously this was ensured whenever we serialize a JSObject/JSArray,
but we can front-load all the checks on the prototypes to the start of
serialization and only check that the prototype is the expected one for
each object.

findings.title: Missing context-less meta-map guard before native_context() call in FastJsonStringifier
findings.message: In `FastJsonStringifier::SerializeObject`, when a JSObject or JSArray is encountered, the code unconditionally calls `obj->map()->map()->native_context()` to retrieve the native context. However, for detached globals (and other objects with context-less meta maps), the meta-map is the read-only `meta_map` root, which has no associated native context. Calling `native_context()` on it triggers a DCHECK failure (`IsNativeContext(*this)`) in `contexts-inl.h`. This was introduced when the fast-path check was refactored to front-load prototype comparisons: the new code obtained the native context early in `SerializeObject` without guarding against context-less meta maps. A malicious page can trigger this via `JSON.stringify` on a detached cross-realm global, causing a crash in debug builds and undefined behavior in release builds.
findings.suggestion: Before calling `native_context()` on the meta-map, check whether it is the context-less read-only `meta_map` root. If it is, bail out to the slow path rather than attempting to dereference a non-existent native context. This is exactly what the fix commit does.

ground_truth.root_cause: A refactor (commit c535aa4) moved the native-context lookup to the beginning of `SerializeObject` to front-load prototype checks for the fast path. The refactored code assumed every JSObject/JSArray would have a meta-map with a native context, which is false for detached globals whose meta-map is the read-only `meta_map` root. No guard was added to handle this case before invoking `native_context()`.
